lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: fixed variable and periodic expenses

objective: Learners classify invented expenses as fixed, variable, or periodic, convert a periodic cost to a monthly equivalent, and total a realistic month.
scenario: Adaeze is an invented seventh grader modelling a pretend month. Fixed costs are $780.00 of housing. Variable costs are $260.00 of food and $145.00 of transport. A periodic invented insurance bill of $720.00 falls once a simulated year. Monthly income is $1,400.00.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Convert Adaeze's invented annual insurance bill into a monthly equivalent.

prompts.text: What is the monthly equivalent of the $720.00 annual bill?

tasks.directions: Total Adaeze's variable costs, then build a full monthly figure that includes fixed, variable, and the periodic equivalent.

prompts.text: What do the variable costs come to?
What is the full monthly cost including the periodic equivalent?

tasks.directions: Compare that with Adaeze's $1,400.00 income, then work out what the month looks like if the periodic bill is ignored until it arrives.

prompts.text: How much is left each month once the periodic equivalent is included?
In the month the $720.00 bill actually lands, what is the net position if nothing was set aside?

tasks.directions: The same bill produced two very different months.

prompts.text: Explain why periodic costs are spread across months in a budget, using Adaeze's two results as evidence.

remediation: If a learner leaves the periodic cost out, have them label every expense fixed, variable, or periodic before any total is computed.
extension: Ask the learner what monthly set-aside would leave Adaeze exactly break-even in the bill month, and to justify it.
